correctness.rationale: Completing the square gives F=(x²−1)(T_n+λ−1)(T_n+λ+1). The two charts glue to a finite locally free rank-two cover of P¹ over the base, with two smooth infinity sections. For generic λ the 2n+2 branch roots are simple and Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus n, hence constant arithmetic genus by flatness. The T_n critical values are ±1 at n−1 simple critical points; the two fixed endpoint roots can collide only with T_n+λ=±1. These two mechanisms exhaust 0,±2, and only double roots occur. At 0 the global square gives two P¹s meeting transversely in n+1 points; each is stable and their first graph Betti number is n. At ±2 the unused T_n-level ±3 provides simple roots and hence integrality. Counting the alternating critical signs and adding the endpoints gives exactly the stated table, including the rational normalization at n=2, λ=−2 (with four preimages of nodes). Each critical root contributes exponent one to the discriminant, each endpoint collision contributes two via the squared resultant; the two shifted T_n factors have constant mutual resultant. This yields exactly the claimed exponents. On the finite chart the total space is the Cayley cubic, whose gradient equations give the four sign points of product 1; at each the Hessian is sign-conjugate to the matrix with 2 on the diagonal and −2 off it, so all are ordinary surface nodes. The smooth infinity sections add none. The independent exact spot check `python3 /workspace/reviews/reproduce_1.py` confirms the discriminant and root counts for n=2–8; the universal conclusion rests on the preceding argument, not that range. No claim at parameter infinity.
